page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg9i.24xlarge is a high clock speed computing instance based on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. Hardware resources include 96 dedicated vCPUs powered by the Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor running at a base frequency of 3.4 GHz. System memory totals 384.0 GB, allocating an even 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Networking capabilities offer a high baseline bandwidth of 48 Gbps, enabling rapid communication in cluster configurations.

The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware accelerators such as GPUs. All storage operations depend on remote network block storage, which relies on the available 48 Gbps network throughput. From a resource density perspective, the absence of local disks reduces host-level storage maintenance while placing high emphasis on external I/O architecture. The dedication of 96 high-frequency cores provides substantial compute throughput without resource contention from shared virtualization models.

The hardware profile aligns with workloads that demand both high-frequency single-thread execution and massive multi-threaded capacity. Common target deployments include large relational databases, in-memory processing pipelines, high-throughput continuous integration systems, data transformation pipelines, and parallel batch processing tasks. Environments requiring balanced memory alongside elevated CPU frequencies can utilize this configuration effectively without provisioning oversized memory instances.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg9i.24xlarge is a high clock speed virtual server instance built on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It provides 96 dedicated vCPUs driven by an Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor operating at a 3.4 GHz clock rate, paired with 384.0 GB of system memory. This configuration maintains a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, supplying 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance lacks bundled local storage and GPUs, necessitating reliance on network-attached block storage for persistence. Network interfaces feature a robust 48 Gbps baseline bandwidth, ensuring significant capacity for data transfer across distributed topologies. With its concentration of elevated clock speeds, high core count, and balanced memory allocation, the ecs.hfg9i.24xlarge delivers strong qualitative compute efficiency for compute-intensive enterprise applications, high-throughput web serving, parallel scientific simulations, and relational database systems requiring substantial CPU performance.
